subject: Pilot readiness: capacity & security gates
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@acme-retail.com>, procure@acme-retail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: capacity & security gates

Hi Anita — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick post-call recap + next steps so we keep momentum for the 4-week pilot. TL;DR: agreed success criteria, sandbox handoff, owners, and two gating items (capacity profile & SOC2 artifacts).

What we agreed (high level)
- Success criteria (see attached spreadsheet): 1) Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms on your representative 512-token prompts; 2) Quality: intent accuracy >= 88% against the evaluation set; 3) Cost: model variant cost target <= $0.80 per 1k tokens for production profile.
- Evaluation plan: Redwood will run 3 scripted runs (baseline, peak, mixed) over your sandbox dataset and share raw logs + summary metrics. You will validate quality with the annotated eval set and provide feedback within 5 business days.
- Ownership
  - Redwood: API sandbox, load test harness, weekly run and summary (Ben).
  - Acme: annotated eval set delivery, acceptance signoff (Anita + Procurement).
  - CS coordination & rollout plan (Marissa).

Two gating items before week 1:
1) Capacity profile: we need your expected concurrency & average prompt sizes. Ben, flag if the attached Load-Profile.csv is sufficient — otherwise we need a quick call to refine.
2) Security artifacts: Acme requested a SOC2 snapshot and the data handling rubric. Marissa will share the SOC2 snapshot and a short KMS/HSM note.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Anita: share the annotated 200-record eval sample and confirm the concurrency numbers by EOD Tue 5/4.
- Ben (Redwood): stand up sandbox endpoints and post one baseline run by Thu 5/6.
- Marissa: upload SOC2 snapshot + short note to the Drive link and ping the procurement thread.

Attachments: POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx (sheet: metrics & acceptance), Load-Profile.csv (sample concurrent patterns)

Notes on integration: we'll provide a curl example for the sandbox (Ben will paste below). If you want a lightweight webhook for streaming tokens, we can enable it in the sandbox but prefer to test non-streaming first for reproducibility.

Thanks — Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
[Attachment: POC-Success-Criteria.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: Load-Profile.csv (csv)]

From: Anita Rao <anita@acme-retail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: capacity & security gates

Kimberly — thanks for the summary, this matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Eval set: we'll deliver a 200-record annotated sample (text + intent tag + expected normalization) by EOD Tue (5/4). Full 2k set will follow within the pilot week once we validate the first run.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state 6 concurrent users with short bursts to 25 for shopping peak tests. Avg prompt length ~420 tokens; max observed ~1200 tokens. I attached a brief note from procurement about timing — they need SOC2 evidence before we can provision any reserved capacity.

Procurement request: if you can surface a SOC2 snapshot and the KMS/HSM summary in Drive, that gets past our internal checklist. Also confirm whether logs can be retained for 30 days in sandbox for our QA team.

We'll accept the proposed success criteria pending the first baseline run. If the baseline shows model selection issues, we'll iterate on model variant choice and quantization profile.

Thanks — Anita

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: capacity & security gates

Adding some technical detail and the sandbox call we'll run this week.
- Sandbox endpoints: /v1/pilot/infer (no streaming) and /v1/pilot/stream (opt-in). We'll seed with a pinned model snapshot (redwood-optimized-1) for the baseline.
- Persistence & logs: sandbox retains request/response logs for 30 days by default; we can extend to 90 on request. Logs include token counts, latencies, and full text payloads (access controlled).
- Load-testing plan: we'll run three scripted jobs: baseline(1x), peak-burst(4x), mixed(30min ramp). We'll provide p50/p95 latency and per-run cost estimate.

Example curl (sandbox — API key redacted):
curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.com/v1/pilot/infer 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-optimized-1","input":"<sample prompt>","max_tokens":512}'

Target acceptance thresholds for the run (internal anchors):
- latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms on the 420-token median prompt;
- throughput: sustained 6 concurrency with peaks to 25 (see Load-Profile.csv);
- cost: estimated token cost target <= $0.80/1k tokens for the candidate model (we'll compare quantized variants if needed);
- quality: we'll compute macro intent accuracy and false positive rate to match your annotated set.

Ben (cc: Marissa for SOC2 handoff). I'll post the first baseline logs on Thu 5/6 and flag any configuration changes needed.

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Load-Profile.csv (csv)]

Hi Anita — following up on SOC2 & procurement asks. I uploaded a short snapshot and KMS note to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-docs (see SOC2-Snapshot.pdf). The snapshot includes a redacted scope and the most recent report date. For Prod we have full attestation; for pilots we provide the snapshot + SOC2 controls summary.

Procurement checklist we can support now:
- SOC2 snapshot: uploaded (SOC2-Snapshot.pdf)
- Logs retention: sandbox defaults to 30 days; we confirm retention and export on request.
- Data encryption: we use customer-managed KMS in Private deployments; hosted pilots use Redwood-managed KMS; details attached.

If procurement needs an NDA or additional redlines, loop in legal and I can coordinate directly. Kimberly — can you confirm whether Acme wants the sandbox to run with streaming off for the first 48 hours? That simplifies metric collection and reduces noise for the evaluation.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2-Snapshot.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks everyone — quick status update from Acme:
- Eval sample: uploaded to the shared Drive (200 annotated rows).
- Concurrency numbers: confirmed (steady 6 / peaks 25).
- Procurement: SOC2 snapshot received, passed initial checklist. Final procurement approval expected by Tue 5/11 pending a short internal review.

Next steps from Acme: wait for Redwood baseline run and summary. We'll aim to provide accept/reject feedback within 3 business days after you post the baseline results. Please nudge if we miss the 5/6 baseline timeline.
